newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak bourse closes lower as Slovnaft shares ease.
newsitem.headline: Slovak bourse closes lower as Slovnaft shares ease.

text.p: The Bratislava Stock Exchange (BSE) closed slightly lower in heavier activity on Monday, pulled down by losses to shares of oil refiner Slovnaft.
Slovnaft lost 10 crowns closing at 790 as the SAX index dipped by 0.12 points to 186.09.
But with only 15 shares traded, brokers said there was no clear further downward trend.

"There are some offers at 830 crowns, what we see as a real market value, but potential investors consider that price as too high and appear to be waiting to buy cheaper," said Dusan Sykora of ING Barings.
On the unlisted floor, drug producer Slovakofarma neared record levels throughout the session with its average price rising 12.83 percent to close at 4,000 crowns.
But dealers said the price had been artificially pushed up to conduct a deal with a larger package, and added that it should fall to more realistic levels of around 3,600 crowns in the near future.
"Slovakofarma is generally a good issue, but its problem is that it is highly illiquid," Sykora said.
Steel producer VSZ led the day's floor trading with 2,521 shares changing hands but closed unchanged at 650.
Overall volume rose to 1,274,405 shares, boosted by large packages traded as direct deals, from 631,968 on Friday. Turnover increased to 1.21 billion crowns from 280.7 million on Friday.
